verdict.rationale: npm documents some first-party portability: users can point npm at any compatible registry or run their own, and lockfiles keep working after switching registries. The registry API also returns package metadata as a JSON document. There is no documented capability to export all of a user's account data in open formats. missing for 10: documented bulk export of account/package data, coverage of private packages and account data, an explicit export or offboarding workflow, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can export all of my data in open formats and leave

citations.quote: You can configure npm to use any compatible registry you like, and even run your own registry.
If you create a lock file while using the default registry you can switch to another registry and npm will install packages from the new registry
This endpoint responds with the package metadata document, sometimes informally called a "packument" or "doc.json".
